subproblems.title: Portmanteau inequalities for vague convergence on an open set
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, (ν_j)_{j∈ℕ} Borel measures on ℝ^P with ν_j(K) < ∞ for every j and every compact K ⊆ U, and μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. If ∫ f dν_j → ∫ f dμ for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ U, then limsup_j ν_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ U and μ(G) ≤ liminf_j ν_j(G) for every open G ⊆ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (νs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → (∀ (j : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → νs j K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, f x ∂(νs j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂μ))) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → limsup (fun j => νs j K) atTop ≤ μ K) ∧ (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → G ⊆ U → μ G ≤ liminf (fun j => νs j G) atTop)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: all measures are Borel measures on ℝ^P. For nonempty A ⊆ ℝ^P, dist(x, A) := inf_{y∈A} |x − y|; thickening(r, A) := {x : dist(x, A) < r} (open; thickening(r, ∅) = ∅) and cthickening(r, A) := {x : dist(x, A) ≤ r} (closed; compact when A is compact, IsCompact.cthickening). This is the expanded form of the Remark in the parent proof: cut-offs from above on compact sets, approximation from inside on open sets. It follows the parent-supplied natural-language proof accepted for node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.convergence_tools-a1.portmanteau-a1. Source: Simon does not print this implication as a separate item. It is the converse of the standard approximation argument that closes the proof of Simon 7.2.4, and step 3 below is the ε-neighbourhood argument by which that proof obtains its (13). Standard reference: Evans–Gariepy, Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions, §1.9 (weak convergence of Radon measures).
1. (Integral versus measure.) Let ρ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P and h : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with 0 ≤ h ≤ 1 and compact support, such that ρ(tsupport h) < ∞. Then h is ρ-integrable: it is measurable, bounded by 1 and zero off tsupport h, which has finite ρ-measure. Since h ≥ 0, ofReal(∫ h dρ) = ∫⁻ ofReal(h) dρ (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). Consequently:
(a) if h = 1 on a closed set B, then ρ(B) ≤ ofReal(∫ h dρ), because 1_B ≤ ofReal ∘ h pointwise and B is Borel;
(b) if h = 0 off a Borel set V, then ofReal(∫ h dρ) ≤ ρ(V), because ofReal ∘ h ≤ 1_V pointwise.
Inequality (b) holds even without the finiteness assumption: if h is not ρ-integrable, then ∫ h dρ = 0 and ofReal(0) = 0 ≤ ρ(V). By hypothesis, ρ(tsupport h) < ∞ holds for ρ = ν_j (every j), and for ρ = μ, whenever tsupport h is a compact subset of U.
2. (Cut-off functions.) For a nonempty compact C ⊆ ℝ^P and r > 0 put h_{C,r}(x) := max(0, 1 − dist(x, C)/r). It is continuous, since dist(·, C) is 1-Lipschitz, and it takes values in [0, 1]. It equals 1 on C, where dist(·, C) = 0. It vanishes off thickening(r, C), since dist(x, C) ≥ r gives 1 − dist(x, C)/r ≤ 0. Hence tsupport h_{C,r} ⊆ closure(thickening(r, C)) ⊆ cthickening(r, C), which is compact, so h_{C,r} has compact support.
3. (Compact sets.) Let K ⊆ U be compact.
If K = ∅, then ν_j(K) = 0 for all j, so limsup_j ν_j(K) = 0 ≤ μ(K).
Otherwise, choose δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open, as U is open and K ⊆ U). Then cthickening(δ, K) is a compact subset of U, so μ(cthickening(δ, K)) < ∞.
Fix r ∈ (0, δ] and h := h_{K,r}. Then tsupport h ⊆ cthickening(r, K) ⊆ cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ U, so h is continuous with compact support and tsupport h ⊆ U.
By step 1(a) with ρ = ν_j and B = K (closed), ν_j(K) ≤ ofReal(∫ h dν_j) for every j. By hypothesis ∫ h dν_j → ∫ h dμ, and ofReal is continuous, so ofReal(∫ h dν_j) → ofReal(∫ h dμ). Therefore
limsup_j ν_j(K) ≤ limsup_j ofReal(∫ h dν_j) = ofReal(∫ h dμ) ≤ μ(cthickening(r, K)).
The last inequality is step 1(b) with ρ = μ and V = cthickening(r, K), which is closed, hence Borel; h = 0 off thickening(r, K) ⊆ V. Thus limsup_j ν_j(K) ≤ μ(cthickening(r, K)) for every r ∈ (0, δ].
Finally, μ(cthickening(r, K)) → μ(closure K) = μ(K) as r → 0⁺ (tendsto_measure_cthickening). It applies because μ(cthickening(δ, K)) < ∞, and closure K = K because K is closed. Letting r ↓ 0 gives limsup_j ν_j(K) ≤ μ(K).
4. (Compact subsets of open sets.) Let G ⊆ U be open and C ⊆ G compact; we show μ(C) ≤ liminf_j ν_j(G). If C = ∅ this is trivial.
Otherwise, choose δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, C) ⊆ G (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and let h := h_{C,δ}. Then h is continuous, 0 ≤ h ≤ 1, h = 1 on C, and h = 0 off thickening(δ, C) ⊆ G. Also tsupport h ⊆ cthickening(δ, C), a compact subset of G ⊆ U.
We combine three facts:
- step 1(a) for ρ = μ, where μ(tsupport h) < ∞ because tsupport h is a compact subset of U;
- the hypothesis ∫ h dν_j → ∫ h dμ, so ofReal(∫ h dν_j) → ofReal(∫ h dμ), and the limit equals the liminf;
- step 1(b) for ρ = ν_j with V = G, which is open, hence Borel.
Together they give
μ(C) ≤ ofReal(∫ h dμ) = lim_j ofReal(∫ h dν_j) = liminf_j ofReal(∫ h dν_j) ≤ liminf_j ν_j(G).
5. (Open sets.) Let G ⊆ U be open. For n ∈ ℕ put C_n := closedBall(0, n) ∖ thickening((n+1)⁻¹, ℝ^P ∖ G). These sets have four properties.
- Each C_n is compact: it is a closed ball minus an open set, hence closed, and it is bounded (ℝ^P is proper).
- C_n ⊆ G: a point of ℝ^P ∖ G has distance 0 to that set, so it lies in thickening((n+1)⁻¹, ℝ^P ∖ G).
- C_n ⊆ C_{n+1}: the balls increase, and the thickenings shrink as the radius (n+1)⁻¹ decreases.
- ⋃_n C_n = G. For x ∈ G pick r > 0 with ball(x, r) ⊆ G and n ≥ |x| with (n+1)⁻¹ ≤ r. If x were in thickening((n+1)⁻¹, ℝ^P ∖ G), there would be y ∉ G with |x − y| < (n+1)⁻¹ ≤ r, i.e. y ∈ ball(x, r) ⊆ G, a contradiction. So x ∈ C_n.
By continuity of μ from below along the increasing sequence (C_n) (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop), μ(G) = lim_n μ(C_n). By step 4, μ(C_n) ≤ liminf_j ν_j(G) for every n. Hence μ(G) ≤ liminf_j ν_j(G) (le_of_tendsto').
Steps 3 and 5 are the two claims. ∎
proof_key_steps: For continuous 0 ≤ h ≤ 1 whose tsupport is a compact subset of U: ρ(B) ≤ ofReal ∫ h dρ if h = 1 on a closed B, and ofReal ∫ h dρ ≤ ρ(V) if h = 0 off a Borel V.
Compact K ⊆ U: with h_{K,r} = 1 on K and tsupport ⊆ cthickening(r, K) ⊆ U, limsup_j ν_j(K) ≤ μ(cthickening(r, K)), which tends to μ(K) as r ↓ 0 (tendsto_measure_cthickening).
Compact C ⊆ open G ⊆ U: with h_{C,δ} = 1 on C and tsupport ⊆ G, μ(C) ≤ lim_j ofReal ∫ h dν_j ≤ liminf_j ν_j(G).
Exhaust G by the increasing compact sets C_n = closedBall(0, n) ∖ thickening((n+1)⁻¹, ℝ^P ∖ G) and use continuity from below.

subproblems.title: Rescaled dilation push-forward λ^{-2}(η_{a,λ})_#μ: finite on compacts, set formula and change of variables
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P that is finite on compact sets, a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. Let η := dilation a λ, η(y) = −(λ^{-1}a) + λ^{-1}y, and ν_λ := η_#(ofReal(λ^{-2})·μ), the push-forward (Measure.map η) of the scalar multiple ENNReal.ofReal(λ^{-2})·μ. Then (i) ν_λ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (ii) ν_λ(S) = ofReal(λ^{-2})·μ(η^{-1}(S)) for every measurable S ⊆ ℝ^P; and (iii) ∫ g dν_λ = λ^{-2}·∫ g(η(x)) dμ(x) (Bochner integrals) for every continuous g : ℝ^P → ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → 0 < lam → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → Measure.map (dilation a lam) (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ 2) • μ) K < ∞) ∧ (∀ S : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet S → Measure.map (dilation a lam) (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ 2) • μ) S = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ 2) * μ (dilation a lam ⁻¹' S)) ∧ ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → ∫ x, g x ∂(Measure.map (dilation a lam) (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ 2) • μ)) = lam⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∫ x, g (dilation a lam x) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Put c := ofReal(λ^{-2}) ∈ [0, ∞), so ν_λ = Measure.map η (c·μ). These are steps 1-4 of the parent proof for one fixed scale λ.
1. (η is a homeomorphism.) Since λ > 0, λ^{-1} ≠ 0. Let e be the homeomorphism Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ^{-1} (y ↦ λ^{-1}•y) followed by Homeomorph.addLeft (−(λ^{-1}•a)) (z ↦ −(λ^{-1}•a) + z). By definition dilationCLM P λ = λ^{-1}•id, so dilationCLM P λ y = λ^{-1}•y. Hence dilation a λ y = −(λ^{-1}•a) + λ^{-1}•y = e(y) for every y, i.e. η = e as functions. Consequently:
- η is continuous, hence Borel measurable (ℝ^P carries its Borel σ-algebra);
- for every compact K, η^{-1}(K) = e^{-1}(K) is compact (Homeomorph.isCompact_preimage), being the image of K under the continuous inverse e.symm.
2. (Proof of (ii).) Let S be measurable. Since η and S are measurable, Measure.map_apply gives ν_λ(S) = (c·μ)(η^{-1}(S)). By the definition of a scalar multiple of a measure (Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul), this equals c·μ(η^{-1}(S)) = ofReal(λ^{-2})·μ(η^{-1}(S)).
3. (Proof of (i).) Let K be compact. In the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, K is closed and therefore measurable, so step 2 gives ν_λ(K) = c·μ(η^{-1}(K)). Here c = ofReal(λ^{-2}) < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top). Also η^{-1}(K) is compact by step 1, so μ(η^{-1}(K)) < ∞ because μ is finite on compact sets. A product of two finite elements of [0, ∞] is finite (ENNReal.mul_lt_top), so ν_λ(K) < ∞.
4. (Proof of (iii).) Let g be continuous.
- Measurability: g is a.e.-strongly measurable for every measure, in particular for ν_λ (Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable), and η is measurable, hence a.e.-measurable for c·μ.
- Change of variables: integral_map gives ∫ g dν_λ = ∫ g(η(x)) d(c·μ)(x).
- Scalar multiple: ∫ f d(c·μ) = c.toReal·∫ f dμ for every function f and every c ∈ [0, ∞] (integral_smul_measure), with no integrability assumption needed. So ∫ g(η(x)) d(c·μ)(x) = c.toReal·∫ g(η(x)) dμ(x).
- Constant: c.toReal = (ofReal(λ^{-2})).toReal = λ^{-2}, because λ^{-2} ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal).
Hence ∫ g dν_λ = λ^{-2}·∫ g(η(x)) dμ(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: dilation a λ coincides with the homeomorphism y ↦ −(λ^{-1}•a) + λ^{-1}•y (smulOfNeZero then addLeft), so η is measurable and η^{-1}(K) is compact for compact K.
Measure.map_apply and Measure.smul_apply give ν_λ(S) = ofReal(λ^{-2})·μ(η^{-1}S) for measurable S.
A compact K is closed, hence measurable; η^{-1}K is compact, so μ(η^{-1}K) < ∞ and ν_λ(K) = ofReal(λ^{-2})·μ(η^{-1}K) < ∞.
integral_map, integral_smul_measure and toReal_ofReal give ∫ g dν_λ = λ^{-2}∫ g∘η dμ for continuous g.
